newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan to post 96/97 net loss due to loan loss.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan to post 96/97 net loss due to loan loss.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp said on Wednesday that it would post a parent net loss in the year ended on March 31, mainly because it earmarked reserves for losses from loans to its subsidiaries.

It concurrently lowered its forecast for its annual dividend in 1996/97 to 4.5 yen per share from the previous forecast of nine yen. The company paid an annual dividend of 16.5 yen per share in 1995/96.
The company said that it expects to post a net loss of 35.9 billion yen in 1996/97. It had previously forecast a net profit of 930 million yen.

Yaohan, the flagship firm of an international retailing group, announced in February a restructuring programme including a reduction of group debt subject to interest payments to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen in the next two years.
The company said later that month that it had agreed with major supermarket chain operator Daiei Inc to sell 16 of its outlets for 33 billion yen.
Yaohan said the sale would make possible the redemption of corporate bonds due in May. The sale would also greatly help it to implement other steps in the restructuring programme, it said.
